newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says Ethiopia holds 15,000 people captive.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says Ethiopia holds 15,000 people captive.

text.p: Sudan said on Wednesday that Ethiopia had taken more than 15,000 people captive since its troops began fighting the Khartoum government in the southern Blue Nile province more than three weeks ago.

"The Ethiopian forces are now holding in captivity more than 10,000 displaced citizens north of Qeissan and some 5,000 at Baba area south of Damazin and east of the Bakkuri areas," Culture and Information Minister Al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohamad Khair told the official Sudan News Agency.
Sudan says Ethiopian and Eritrean troops are fighting alongside rebels who are waging an offensive in the east and south. Both countries deny any involvement in the conflict.

The rebels, who started their campaign on January 12, say they control most of the Blue Nile province but the government only concedes to the fall of a few towns including the key border towns of Kurmuk and Qeissan.

Khair said the Ethiopians had prevented relief aid from reaching the displaced and charged international humanitarian relief agencies of being "strangely silent about the inhumane practices perpetrated by the Ethiopians such as killing, torture and rape".

Sudan's provincial Blue Nile government says it expects at least 35,000 people to be displaced because of the fighting which has mostly taken place in the east and south of the province as rebels are threatening to take a strategic dam.

The Swiss-based charity Christian Solidarity International (CSI) said in a report this month that Sudanese government forces had "bombed and torched" villages across the Blue Nile area near the Ethiopian border.
It said at least 50,000 people had been forced to flee from their homes and that some were living in makeshift shelters or out in the open.
